title: Handler Escapes
warm:
Handler escapes meant [player_name] watched the hangar endgame tear open and Nolan Greer choose the hunt while she waited across the hall—twelve steps of Crownspire geography become both refuge and evidence. Early thirties, she/her, neighbor-mistress—Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose without a settled body. Vivienne's four fates stayed open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging. An escape did not force any of them.

"I hunt," Nolan said, mid-forties finance and tech, brutal charm scraped raw, cufflinks loud as the black car peeled from the curb. "You wait across the hall. Soft alibi stays soft by not chasing plane fuel into worse paper. Brooks gets colder without needing you in the hangar when the handler runs."

Marcus Pell's traveling language scattered into radio static. Rhea Quinn's slate downstairs still thinned. Unused perfume still breathed from the master bath she should not know. Wind sheer threw city light as accusation across her own threshold. Elevator chime trembled. Soft still meant pliable evidence wearing neighbor walls.

She catalogued the wait the way Brooks would: door closed, light on, soft cover holding while money hunted. Layer 9 made every hush a held breath. Hope and dread shared the hallway. Nolan's hand on her doorframe—protective, unfinished, a promise that was not marriage.

"Vivienne returned spends the hunt into a door that might open," he murmured. "Open secret spends the escape into Crownspire noise we endure together. Neither locks her fate. Both spend us into endings that leave four doors open."

Wine rings on her own marble. Black car gone. [player_name] felt the across-the-hall wait fitting her mouth like expensive silk and understood that letting Nolan hunt while she held soft would change which silence she could still claim—without forcing Vivienne into any single fate.
